proposal.observation: Round-1 feedback: relaxing the oblique Hough (threshold 30, maxLineGap 70) and lowering curvature_threshold to 0.0004 left the binarised outlier map visually unchanged and did NOT raise oblique line yield (still ~8 short oblique segments vs ~30 horizontal fallback segments; one green segment at x~1450 was even lost, consistent with HoughLinesP sampling noise). The only material change was in prompt centres: the ring at x~1630 lost its detected negative_slope centre (y~370) and fell back to an 'assume' centre at y~1130, and correspondence_f1@15 dropped 0.365 -> 0.273 with sam_fill_rate, ring_count_error and depth_nan_ratio unchanged. So the proxy is highly sensitive to WHERE each ring's K-block prompt centre lands, and 7 of 12 centres are still 'assume' at alternating y~1130 / y~1550, i.e. inferred from the pattern prior rather than from detected intersections. The two complete oblique pairs that do exist give a direct geometric read of the K block: pair at x 2200-2560 spans y 1243 -> 1480 (~237 px) and pair at x 2830-3200 spans 3738 -> 3990 (~252 px), i.e. K height ~1220 mm at 5 mm/px, and slopes of 6.3-10.3 deg (mean ~9 deg). Several detected oblique segments (x~1380-1440 y~440, x~1350-1380 y~1290) intersect vertical joints but were discarded by the distance-pattern check rather than becoming prompt centres.
proposal.rule: d8: m_spacing_regularity poor vs K/AB pattern -> f_pattern_mismatch (detected intersections rejected by check_distance_pattern, replaced by 'assume' centres). d7 was tested in round 1 and r_relax_hough was inert on this scan, so the enhancing/Hough lever is ruled out; apply r_fix_height_priors instead: set K_height (which derives K_height_pixel for the pattern check and the SAM template) and taper angle from the measured block geometry and widen pattern_tolerance so detected intersections are accepted, plus a modest binary_threshold reduction to thicken the dotted joint strokes feeding the intersection step.
proposal.failure_mode: stage_4_detection.f_pattern_mismatch -> stage_5_segmentation.f_crop_offset (prompt centres assumed, not detected; block templates land off the true K position)
proposal.rationale: Round 1 showed that on 4-1 the line-yield lever (curvature_threshold, oblique Hough threshold/gap) does not change the outlier map or oblique yield, while the position of K prompt centres moves correspondence_f1@15 by ~0.09 per ring. The remaining lever inside bounds that decides whether a detected intersection becomes a prompt centre is the distance-pattern check (K_height_pixel, AB_height_pixel, pattern_tolerance). Setting sam.K_height=1220 mm matches the K height measured directly from the two complete oblique pairs (237-252 px at 5 mm/px), so both the pattern prior and the SAM K template match the real block; sam.angle=9.0 matches the mean measured taper of the detected oblique edges (6.3-10.3 deg); detecting.pattern_tolerance=18 (bounds 5-20) lets near-miss intersections such as those at x~1630 and x~1270 pass the pattern check instead of degrading to 'assume'; detecting.binary_threshold=115 slightly thickens the dotted chevron strokes so the existing oblique segments extend to the vertical joints. This follows the improving dev analogue s021 in direction for K_height (1120) and angle (11.8, upper range) while staying near the geometry read off this scan. Unfolding (clean unroll, orient_agreement 0.94) and denoising (nan ratio unaffected by round 1) are left untouched to avoid the ring_count_error breakage seen in s005/s016. Joint outcome expected; no per-parameter attribution claimed; all values inside configs/bounds/complex.json.
